feedback:
Written before this candidate has raced. Evidence: iteration 1 (best, 52.8) used x = ±0.03 with 16 mm footprints, kp 1.5, kd 0.1, base_speed 1.4, and went off track on all 60 trials with one line-loss event and max_error of 0.061 to 0.065 m. Iteration 0 (x = ±0.04, 12 mm, kp 2.0, kd 0.05, base_speed 1.6) scored 26 with the same failure. The sensor geometry explains this: a 16 mm footprint sees the 25 mm tape only while the robot centre is within about 0.0205 m of the line, so the outer sensor at ±0.03 is lost at about 0.05 m offset. The candidate's ±0.05 spread should keep the outer sensor on tape out to about 0.07 m, which is the mechanism to test, and the geometry itself is valid.

The problem is that the candidate is not an isolated test. Its rationale says it is the only change against iteration 1, but kp went from 1.5 back to 2.0 and kd from 0.1 to 0.15. The rationale also says the Evaluator recommended kp 2.0 and kd 0.15, but my iteration 1 guidance was kp 1.5 with kd raised only if line loss persisted. If the next race improves, we cannot tell whether the wider spread or the higher gains caused it. If it worsens, the gain change could be the cause and the geometry may be fine. Keep the controller at the iteration 1 values so the sensor change is measured on its own.

Next-race guidance: if line_loss_events falls to 0 or 1 and max_error drops below 0.06 m, keep the spread and then test base_speed 1.6 for completion time. If rms_error rises above about 0.04 m, the coarser signal from the wider spread is the likely cause, so test sensor_size 0.012 with the same spread. If one line-loss event remains with max_error above 0.06 m, the controller is limiting, so test kd 0.15 as a separate change.
requested_changes: Revert controller.kp from 2.0 to 1.5 and controller.kd from 0.15 to 0.1 (the iteration 1 values), so the only change against the best raced design (iteration 1, 52.8) is the sensor spread.

Keep sensor_positions at x = +0.05, +0.025, 0, -0.025, -0.05 with y = 0.03 and sensor_size 0.016, since the iteration 1 outer sensor was lost at about 0.05 m offset and the wider spread should extend reach to about 0.07 m.
Keep base_speed 1.4 and line_loss last_direction, so that any change in completion or completion_time after the race can be attributed to the sensor change alone.
